Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'not yet' or 'not there yet' (未在). Across the Chan corpus it is especially frequent as a master's verdict on a reply, shout, verse, or claimed understanding: Zhaozhou says, 'Not there yet; say more' (未在更道); another exchange records, 'You have got it, but you are still not there yet' (你也得只是未在); and an unnamed elder repeatedly waves a visitor away with, 'Not there yet, not there yet; go for now' (未在未在且去). The same words retain their ordinary temporal force in 'Even if you reached a thousand years, you still would not yet be old' (直至千歲也未在). Thus the corpus deploys one literal phrase both as an evaluative reply and in ordinary statements of something not yet reached or completed.
Senses.Note: The exact headword occurs 1,038 times in 230 allowlisted texts. No defining formula of the forms 'the so-called not-there-yet' (所謂未在), 'it is called not-there-yet' (謂之未在 or 名為未在), or 'what is meant by not-there-yet?' (何謂未在) was found. The repeated collocation 'not there yet; say more' (未在更道) occurs 72 times in 39 texts, while 'you have got it, but are still not there yet' (你也得只是未在) and the repeated dismissal 'not there yet, not there yet; go for now' (未在未在且去) display two further recorded shapes. The subject left incomplete is sometimes named, as in 'the matter beyond is not there yet' (向上事未在).
